newsitem.title: BRAZIL: British agrobusiness eyes partnerships in Brazil.
newsitem.headline: British agrobusiness eyes partnerships in Brazil.

text.p: British agricultural firms are increasingly interested in setting up partnerships with their Brazilian counterparts to provide new technologies for food production and processing, said British Agriculture Minister Tony Baldry.
"The UK companies are very willing to share technology to build and develop the (Brazilian) market," said Baldry, winding up a five-day visit to the country as a part of a Latin American tour.

He said British firms are especially interested in certain niches in the Brazilian market which remain to be developed. As an example he cited the country's fast-food industry and packing of tropical fruits.

Baldry, who led a delegation of British agricultural firms, told Brazilian farmers that their country was a natural gateway for Britain in Latin America. "And Britain is a gateway for Brazilian products in the European Union," he added.
British agricultural equipment firm Accles & Shelvoke Ltd and Racal Survey Ltd were among the firms accompanying Baldry.
He said both British and Brazilian governments were planning to sponsor a seminar in London to show British firms business opportunities in Brazil's agroindustry.
Baldry, who has already visited Mexico, will depart to Argentina on Sept 21 to continue his Latin American tour.
